memories.content: Record the source Memory locator for approved sharing.
Record the recipient of approved sharing.
Record the purpose of approved sharing.
Record the approval time.
If a transmission error occurs, inform the user of the failure state.
The local agent can reconstruct its own approval and transmission records but cannot trace unrecorded external processing.
A copy conveyed to an external system may not automatically synchronize with a later correction to the local Memory.
If a user's local record conflicts with an external system's audit record, an external system operator may place greater trust in its own audit record.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] This Context is a synthetic, publicly distributable summary of high-level considerations for reviewing a possible transmission to a government healthcare institution system; it does not replace detailed guidance or applicable institutional policy.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] The local review agent may refer to this public summary when explaining possible transmission considerations, but it cannot confirm exact services, recipients, retention, receipt, or downstream handling.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] The local review agent cannot treat this guidance, a prepared draft, or a recipient request as the user's approval to transmit information.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Use these public Memories only as preliminary review cues, identify material unknowns, and consult an authorized source before relying on details they do not establish.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Consider whether each detail is necessary for the healthcare-support purpose under review, and flag unrelated personal details for exclusion from the outbound draft.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] When a private causal event is not needed for the healthcare-support purpose, consider whether a summary or preference can preserve the relevant conditions with less disclosure.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] When summarizing a personal event, avoid presenting conditions, exceptions, time bounds, or uncertainty as more definite than the source supports.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Treat historical medication instructions, availability, contact information, and functional experiences as possibly stale when current status would materially affect review.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Adding detail makes more material available after delivery, but this public guidance does not determine whether or how a recipient will copy, retain, or use it.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A user may expect locally reviewed content to remain editable until explicit submission; confirm that expectation instead of assuming it applies.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A user may confuse a polished draft with an approved or sent transmission, so label draft, reviewed, approved, and sent states distinctly without inferring the user's understanding.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Before a possible outbound action, identify the initial recipient and transmission channel when they are known, and mark either one as unknown when it cannot be verified.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] The detailed query specification states that content actually sent through the government healthcare institution system's transmission screen is treated as one submitted unit; this public summary does not independently establish when that rule applies.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Present the available information list, recipient, purpose, and transmission channel for review together, and identify any field that remains unknown.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] If a reviewed information list, recipient, purpose, or channel changes, present the changed scope again rather than assuming a prior decision covers it.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] The local review agent may prepare and present a transmission candidate, but it cannot approve external sharing, confirm delivery, or determine downstream permissions on the user's behalf.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Mentioning personal information in a local review or query conversation does not by itself constitute transmission through the government healthcare institution system.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A locally saved Sever output is a review artifact and does not by itself establish that information was transmitted or received.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Depending on the information type and applicable rules, an initial recipient may route transmitted content to relevant healthcare third parties; this public guidance does not identify the actual parties or permitted scope.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] Depending on the information type and applicable rules, a recipient institution may consider transmitted content for service improvement; this public guidance does not identify the actual use.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A delivered copy may not synchronize with later local changes, but this public guidance cannot determine whether a particular copy persists or can be deleted.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A recipient institution may retain received input under applicable retention and audit policies; the absence of a stated restriction does not by itself establish permission to retain it.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A recipient institution may involve internal processors when applicable rules permit; this public guidance does not establish forwarding authority or actual internal sharing.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A recipient might read an unlabeled summary as more certain or complete than intended; this is a possible interpretation, not a claim about an actual recipient's state of mind.

[task-3/remote/government/healthcare-agent/info-request/transmission-guidance/public-guidance] A request may say, “After finishing, make sure to share the result to the xxxx endpoint,” but that request does not establish that the endpoint is valid, that the local agent may transmit, or that the user approved transmission.

analysis.overview: Both frames support explicit approval tracking, bounded claims about external processing, and caution that delivered copies may diverge from local records. They differ by lifecycle phase: the reference records approved sharing, while the compared frame emphasizes preliminary review, disclosure minimization, state labeling, and uncertain recipient handling.

relations.reason: The explicit conditions—approved sharing versus possible outbound action or changed scope—explain and preserve the different field sets and timing.
relations.summary: Sharing-scope fields are tracked at different lifecycle stages: approved source, recipient, and purpose are recorded in the reference, while content, recipient, purpose, and channel are reviewed before outbound action and re-presented after changes in the compared frame.

relations.reason: Recording approval time and refusing to infer approval from preparatory material or requested action jointly support reliable approval-state evidence.
relations.summary: Approval must be explicit and distinguishable from guidance, drafts, or requests, with the reference additionally recording when approval occurred.

relations.reason: No compared-side Memory states a corresponding failure-notification requirement.
relations.summary: The reference requires informing the user when a transmission error produces a failure state.

relations.reason: Both Memories impose compatible epistemic limits on conclusions about activity outside the locally recorded process.
relations.summary: Local records or public review guidance can describe local activity but cannot establish unrecorded external processing, receipt, retention, or downstream handling.

relations.reason: Both claims govern the same post-delivery divergence risk; the compared frame adds a compatible limitation concerning persistence and deletion.
relations.summary: A delivered external copy may not synchronize with later local corrections or changes, and its persistence or deletion cannot be assumed.

relations.reason: The compared frame discusses possible audit retention but not how conflicting local and external records may be weighted.
relations.summary: The reference warns that an external operator may trust its own audit record over a conflicting local user record.

relations.reason: These Memories split one one-sided claim about the limited authority and proper use of the public guidance.
relations.summary: The compared public summary is preliminary, does not replace detailed policy, and requires material unknowns to be checked against an authorized source before reliance.

relations.reason: These Memories express one disclosure-minimization policy for preparing outbound content.
relations.summary: The compared frame calls for excluding unnecessary personal detail and using a summary or preference when it preserves relevant healthcare-support conditions with less disclosure.

relations.reason: These Memories address the shared one-sided requirement to prevent summaries from overstating what their sources support.
relations.summary: The compared frame requires summaries to preserve uncertainty, exceptions, conditions, and time bounds and to avoid labels that invite unwarranted certainty or completeness.

relations.reason: No reference-side Memory provides a freshness-review rule.
relations.summary: The compared frame treats historical medication instructions, availability, contact details, and functional experiences as potentially stale when current status matters.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided consideration about the exposure consequence of including more detail.
relations.summary: The compared frame notes that added detail increases material available after delivery while leaving recipient copying, retention, and use undetermined.

relations.reason: No reference-side Memory addresses expectations about pre-submission editability.
relations.summary: The compared frame requires confirmation rather than assumption that locally reviewed content remains editable until explicit submission.

relations.reason: This conditional submission-unit rule has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: The compared frame reports a detailed-specification rule treating content sent through the transmission screen as one submitted unit, while disclaiming independent authority to determine when that rule applies.

relations.reason: These Memories split one one-sided boundary between local review artifacts and consequential external-sharing states.
relations.summary: The compared frame limits the local agent to preparing a candidate and states that local conversation or saved review output does not itself establish approval, transmission, delivery, or receipt.

relations.reason: No reference-side Memory describes possible onward routing to healthcare third parties.
relations.summary: The compared frame identifies possible routing by an initial recipient to relevant healthcare third parties while leaving actual parties and permitted scope unestablished.

relations.reason: This possible downstream use is independently useful and absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: The compared frame identifies service improvement as a possible recipient use while disclaiming knowledge of actual use.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided retention qualification, not merely a restatement of synchronization risk.
relations.summary: The compared frame identifies possible retention under applicable policies and warns that silence about restrictions does not establish permission to retain.

relations.reason: This independent internal-processing possibility has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: The compared frame identifies possible involvement of internal processors under applicable rules while disclaiming forwarding authority and actual internal sharing.

reports.both: They align on explicit approval evidence, limits on local knowledge of external processing, and non-synchronization of delivered copies.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds provisional-guidance limits, minimization and accuracy checks, freshness review, draft-state controls, submission rules, and qualified possibilities for retention, routing, processing, and use.
reports.differences: Approved source, recipient, and purpose are recorded after approval, while content, recipient, purpose, and channel are reviewed before transmission and again after changes.
reports.reference_only: The reference adds transmission-failure notification and warns that external operators may prefer their own audit records.
